cell-background: Use case: scientific-educational. Produce original raster educational game art for grades9–10. Style reference is the supplied invented drawing aesthetic: macabre anatomical cabinet, rich oil-painted specimen realism, dark umber ground, crimson muscle, luminous ivory tendons and bone, amber highlights, tiny restrained aged parchment labels. Use modern textbook/poster explanatory hierarchy with clearly located enlargements and intentionally enlarged teaching detail. No gore or wounds, no surgical tools, no decorative clutter. Portrait 1024x1536. Keep lower 55% entirely dark clean umber ground, absolutely no anatomy or text there; this is useful play space. Art occupies upper45% only. Uppermost 60px also quiet. A small cell cutaway at upper left, its closed lipid bilayer boundary with clear fluid interior and an empty nucleus destination. A fine locator line leads from one edge of the membrane to an enlarged lipid bilayer at upper right: two rows of water-loving golden heads facing out, paired dark tails meet in the middle. A restrained heading reads 'INSIDE / OUTSIDE'. Only labels 'water', 'membrane', 'enlarged edge'. This scene explains boundaries; do not paint a nucleus in the cell.

ONE complete arm anatomical model, not two arms. Arm centered in upper45%, scapula at upper center, upper arm points vertically down, elbow at y430 then forearm bends diagonally up right toward a small hand at y290. Bone ivory; biceps a distinct crimson spindle along right/front of humerus, triceps along left/back. Clearly continuous ivory tendons from biceps to scapula and radius at front of elbow; triceps tendon continues onto olecranon behind elbow, origin on scapula/humerus. Include distinct enlarged small bone-matrix windows in radius and ulna, gold mineral among fibres. Minimal heading 'PULL / SUPPORT'. Labels only 'biceps', 'triceps', 'radius', 'ulna'. All arm anatomy inside x230..790,y100..650; clear space either side. No secondary arm, no separate muscle specimen. This exact complete image will be mechanically separated into aligned muscle and mineral fittings: keep muscle bellies visually isolated from bone, and tendon endpoints unambiguous.

cell-atlas: Use case: scientific-educational. A production sprite atlas of original anatomy teaching illustrations in the invented reference aesthetic: luminous oil-painted specimens, crimson muscle, amber fluid, ivory membranes and bone, rich tangible material, unusual macabre cabinet mood without gore. Grade9–10 textbook clarity and exaggerated teaching details. ISOLATED OBJECTS ON ACTUAL TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND. No text, no labels, no grid, no panels, no shadows stretching between cells. Exactly 3 equal columns and 4 equal rows on a square 1536x1536 canvas; each object fully enclosed within its cell and 60px empty gutters all round. Row-major order exactly as follows. Row1: (1) cluster of six phospholipid molecules with round golden heads and two dark flexible tails each; (2) clear water droplet with three enlarged water molecules beside it; (3) coiled DNA double helix, pearl gold and deep red. Row2: (4) empty round nuclear envelope cutaway with pores, clearly hollow; (5) complete nucleus cutaway with DNA inside and short RNA thread emerging; (6) empty spherical cell membrane bag cutaway with clear fluid and bilayer edge, empty center suitable for overlaying nucleus later. Row3: (7) several separate elongated crimson muscle precursor cells, each containing parallel fibres and a small nucleus; (8) ivory-gold bone mineral crystals beside a porous bone chip; (9) small cluster of translucent paired-tail lipids. Row4: (10) single golden membrane pore cutaway; (11) delicate ivory bundled tendon fibres; (12) single completed nucleus exactly matching object5, small and rounded.

Row1: (1) outer ear with canal only and open inner end; (2) thin pearly eardrum membrane isolated oval; (3) outer ear with canal terminated by pearly eardrum. Row2: (4) exactly three tiny linked ossicle bones; (5) outer ear canal eardrum and linked ossicles complete, no cochlea; (6) amber spiral cochlear chamber cutaway filled with blue grey fluid, no sensory inset. Row3: (7) enlarged tissue strip of attached sensory cells with short hair bundles, overlying membrane and yellow nerve contacts, never floating; (8) cochlea with a clearly linked enlargement of sensory tissue; (9) complete outer ear canal eardrum bones and cochlea in one continuous section, no nerve. Row4: (10) golden branching hearing nerve leading toward small pale brain outline; (11) cochlea with hearing nerve leading toward pale brain outline, no outer ear; (12) complete ear canal eardrum ossicles cochlea and nerve leading toward pale brain outline. Show no duplicated organs or random loose bits.
